title: Sanitize and Harden Eval Harness for Deterministic Load Tests
creator: Anya Patel
description: Problem: The eval/load/perf harness exhibits intermittent flakiness and non-deterministic outputs across CI runs. Root causes we've observed include: (1) mixed tokenizer implementations between legacy python runner and new rust/golang shim causing different byte-level sequences; (2) RNG seeding inconsistencies across multiprocessing workers; (3) minor dependency drift (numpy/tqdm/torch) producing slight performance and numeric variance; (4) CI images with different cuda/cuDNN minor versions across runners; (5) flaky KV cache reuse tests and race conditions when tracing workload latencies. Context: This ticket is a focused engineering cleanup to reduce noise in regression signals and make perf runs reproducible enough to automate regression gating.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end synthetic regression runs reproduce identical token sequences given the same seed for 99.9% of sampled prompts
CI nightly and PR flame jobs pass with <1% variance in 95th percentile latency across 5 consecutive runs
All test containers pinned to approved base image (rwinf-base:2025-01) in CI manifests
Dependency matrix pinned or shimmed: numpy==1.25.x, torch==2.2.x (or compatible), tokenizers pinned + compatibility layer verified
KV cache reuse and prefix-caching unit tests converted from timing-based assertions to state/assertion-based checks
New lightweight smoke-runner (go binary) added and runs in <20s for quick feedback in PRs
Documentation updated: runbook for reproducing flakiness and instructions for adding deterministic scenarios
